title: land is associative
statement: For every natural a, b, c: land(land(a, b), c) = land(a, land(b, c)).

formal.statement: ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.land (AxNat.land x0 x1) x2) (AxNat.land x0 (AxNat.land x1 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Nat.land_assoc is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- land_assoc 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.land_assoc[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type -- producing this row at all is a machine-checked proof. `nat_theorem_inventory` exits non-zero for a name that does not exist, and `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count decides the exit status. Anchored with `^Nat\.land_assoc[[:space:]]` so a sibling name cannot satisfy this row. Run `--release` -- the debug build of this inventory example SIGABRTs on stack depth (unrelated to this proof).

evidence.supports: land(land(3, 7), 5) = land(3, land(7, 5)) = 1, with BOTH intermediate values (land(3,7)=3, land(7,5)=5) genuinely NONZERO -- the fully-generic sub-case of the hard leaf (both nested landAux applications stuck, neither settling for the easy zero-corner), not a degenerate instance a wrong proof of the easy leaves alone could pass.
evidence.notes: Applies `Nat.land_assoc` symbolically (against free `a`, `b`, `c`) and at the concrete instance `(a, b, c) = (3, 7, 5)`, confirming the admitted type matches `Eq (land (land 3 7) 5) (land 3 (land 7 5))`, that `land 3 7` and `land 7 5` are each nonzero (non-vacuity of the hard-leaf exercise), and that both sides compute to `1`.

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*); `x0`/`x1`/`x2` are `a`/`b`/`c`.

Built on `Nat.land_aux_assoc_of_fuel : forall fuel a b c, landAux fuel (landAux fuel a b) c = landAux fuel a (landAux fuel b c)`, itself proved by `agree_by_double_fuel_induction`, unconditional in `fuel` (landAux's fuel-exhaustion row is the absorbing constant 0). Four prior lanes traced this derivation without building it (`docs/plan/status/247-nat-bitwise-assoc.md`, `252-nat-assoc-dichotomy.md`, `257-nat-land-assoc-impl.md`); this lane executed the fully-worked plan in `257`, verifying every traced step against the actual `guarded`/`land_aux_agree_of_fuel`/`land_aux_eq_zero_of_left_eq_zero` signatures rather than trusting the prose. The step case splits `c`, then `b`, then `a` (per `257`'s own correction of an earlier `a,b,c` order, cross-checked here again against `guarded`'s n-outermost guard). The hard leaf (`a,b,c` all positive) dichotomizes the two nested `landAux` values (`Y` first, then `X` within `Y != 0`) via `Nat.zero_or_succ`: the `Y = 0` case mirrors `Nat.land_aux_eq_zero_of_left_eq_zero` via `Nat.land_aux_comm_of_fuel`; the `Y != 0, X = 0` case applies that same propagation lemma directly; the fully generic `Y != 0, X != 0` case reconstructs BOTH nested values' own div/mod decomposition via `Nat.div_mod_unique`/`Nat.div_mod_exec` and closes via the outer induction's own `ih` (for the recursive halves) plus `Nat.mul_assoc` (for the per-bit product) -- no new arithmetic lemma beyond what the propagation lemma already used.

`Nat.land_assoc` itself re-fuels through the shared fuel `F := add(a, b)` (NOT `a+b+c` -- `c` never needs its own `Le` bound, since `Nat.land_aux_agree_of_fuel`'s hypotheses constrain only the `m` position, never `n`), following `Nat.land_comm`'s exact bookkeeping pattern one argument wider.

This is the `Nat.land` twin of Mathlib v4.30's `Nat.land_assoc` (`F:ml430-nat-land-assoc-ad4775b8`, flipped alongside this fact) -- our `Nat.land` is itself proved equal to Mathlib's `bitwise and` specialization by `Nat.bitwise_and_eq_land` (`nat_prelude/rec_agreement.rs`), so this closes the same proposition Mathlib states, not a lookalike about a different definition.
